newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil firms but rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil firms but rangebound.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps firmed late afternoon on Wednesday on selective buying from some traders looking for bargains, brokers said.
"There was some buying when the market fell to around the $25.50 (per barrel) mark," one broker said.
March swaps were last quoted at $25.90/$26.00 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $25.55/$25.65.
Brokers said the market traded in the morning at $25.62, $25.65 and $25.70 per barrel and in the afternoon at $25.85 and $25.90.
The March/April time spread widened slightly due to the stronger front month and traded at 20 cents per barrel, brokers said.
Traders said the market is rangebound at $25.50-26.00 per barrel.
"The Chinese buyers came out to buy when the market falls to around $25.50," one trader said.
Chinese buying interest is said to have boosted sentiment as some players took it as a cue for China's imminent return to buy physical cargoes.
Most players said China has yet to emerge to buy physical gas oil in a big way and some of the recent swap purchases were more "wishful thinking" rather than real demand.

Fuel oil edged up slightly on talks of prompt demand in the local physical market. March swaps traded in the afternoon at $103.50 per tonne and was last quoted at $103.00/$104.00, up about 25 cents from Tuesday.
